policy_title: Introduce urgent pay review for armed forces
stated: Reform UK will introduce an urgent pay review to increase basic pay across the armed forces to boost recruitment and retention, stating that a private soldier is paid less than an Amazon worker.

source.quote: Introduce Urgent Pay Review Increase basic pay across our armed forces to boost recruitment and retention. It is unacceptable that a private soldier is paid less than an Amazon worker.

bearing_set.reason: Directly targets pay levels for a specific workforce (armed forces), with stated intent to raise basic pay and address recruitment/retention — a clear fair-pay intervention.
Recruitment and retention of armed forces personnel directly affects national security and defence posture — a core O5 indicator.

A service-wide pay uplift for ~150,000+ regular personnel represents material additional public expenditure; if unfunded, it concretely worsens the 'is spending funded vs borrowed' and debt-path indicators.

membership_note: Three clear bearings: the direct pay effect (O4), the defence-readiness effect (O5), and the fiscal cost (O12). Inequality (O14) effect would be negligible at national scale; broader prosperity (O13) linkage is too indirect to clear the non-negligible bar.
